name: Reaction-Advection
desc: Gray-Scott Turing chemistry running inside a moving fluid — every step the reagents are advected along a divergence-free curl field before they react, so the spots are never allowed to sit still: they stretch into streaming comet filaments, shear, fold and tear apart, then re-nucleate downstream while feed and kill march the chemistry through spots, worms and mitosis over minutes; vivid streaming reagents, ironbow thermal, edge-lit radiograph, verdigris patina on bronze, or silky graphite.

energy.doc: brightness + colour gain of the reagent field

scale.doc: magnification into a sub-region of the reactor — guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: reaction steps/frame + flow evolution rate (0.2 still streams)

density.doc: number and size of the drifting injectors that keep seeding fresh reagent (this is what stops the chemistry dying out)

peclet.doc: Peclet number — advection vs diffusion. 0 collapses to plain isotropic Gray-Scott; 1 shreds every spot into long streaming filaments. THE knob of this piece

feed.doc: Gray-Scott feed rate — with kill, selects the regime (spots / worms / maze / mitosis); it also marches slowly on its own

kill.doc: Gray-Scott kill rate — the other half of the regime coordinate

hue.doc: primary hue anchoring the reagent ramp

x.doc: horizontal pan + the centre of the global swirl

y.doc: vertical pan + the centre of the global swirl

style.doc: aesthetic: vivid streaming reagents / ironbow thermal / edge-lit radiograph / verdigris patina on bronze / silky flow-shaded graphite

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the initial nucleation, the flow and the injectors
